newsitem.title: USA: Most Americans say too few tax cuts in budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Most Americans say too few tax cuts in budget deal.

text.p: Most Americans believe the new plan to balance the federal budget doesn't cut taxes enough and is not fair to the middle class, according to a new poll released on Friday.

The Time/CNN poll showed that 65 percent of respondents felt the agreement between President Clinton and the Republican-controlled Congress to balance the budget contains too few tax cuts. Some 20 percent said the proposed tax cuts were too severe, and 15 percent were unsure.

The budget deal contains a net tax cut of $85 billion, including a $500 per child tax credit, a broad-based capital gains tax cut, relief from estate taxes paid on inheritances worth more than $600,000, and a tax break to help pay for higher education worth $35 billion over five years.
Half of those polled said the budget deal does not cut government spending enough, against 37 percent who said it does and 13 percent who were not sure.

Some 53 percent of respondents said the budget deal was not fair to the middle class, and 52 percent said it was not fair to "someone like them." Sixty-one percent said, however, that the deal was fair to wealthy Americans.
The poll of 1,017 people was conducted by telephone on May 7-8 and has a margin of error of 3.1 percent.
